answer_points: Lipase digests fat (lipid). Breakdown is accepted for digest.
Which are acidic, lowering the pH of the mixture, or making the mixture more acidic.
worked_example.question:
5 cm³ of milk B and 1 cm³ of lipase were added to a test tube.

The pH of this mixture was pH 7.

This test tube was placed in a water bath for 10 minutes.

The pH of the mixture changed from pH 7 to pH 5.

Explain what caused this change in pH.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each link in the chain: lipase, fatty acids, lower pH.

key_idea: Carbohydrases, proteases and lipases break food down into small soluble molecules. Bile helps lipase by neutralising stomach acid and emulsifying fat. The small molecules are used to build new carbohydrates, lipids and proteins.

blocks.text: Digestive enzymes convert food into small soluble molecules that can be absorbed into the blood. Each type acts on one type of food.
Carbohydrases break down carbohydrates to simple sugars. Amylase is the carbohydrase that breaks down starch.

diagram.alt: Sort each statement into amylase, protease or lipase.

items: Amylase: starch to sugars. Protease: protein to amino acids. Lipase: fat to fatty acids and glycerol.
The pancreas and small intestine make all three types.
Each product is small and soluble, so it can be absorbed.

sections.heading: The three types of digestive enzyme

blocks.text: Bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder. It is released into the small intestine, where it helps lipase.

items.meaning: Breaking large droplets of fat into many small droplets.

items: Bile is alkaline. It neutralises the hydrochloric acid that comes from the stomach.
This gives the correct pH for the enzymes in the small intestine.
Bile emulsifies fat. This gives small droplets with a larger surface area.
The alkaline conditions and the large surface area increase the rate of fat breakdown by lipase.

diagram.alt: How bile helps fat digestion: bile is released into the small intestine, neutralises acid, emulsifies fat into small droplets, giving a larger surface area, so lipase breaks the fat down faster.
steps: Bile released into the small intestine
Acid neutralised: correct pH for lipase

items: Bile is made in the liver, stored in the gall bladder and is alkaline.
It emulsifies fat, which increases the surface area for lipase.
Bile does not digest fat. Lipase does.

blocks.text: The small molecules from digestion are absorbed into the blood. The body uses them to build new molecules, and some are used in respiration.

rows: Carbohydrates, such as starch and cellulose

items.meaning: A small molecule that joins with many others to make a polymer, for example an amino acid.
A large molecule made of many monomers joined together, for example a protein.

items: Some glucose is used in respiration.
Amino acids are joined to make the proteins the body needs for growth, such as muscle.
When lipase breaks down fat in milk, fatty acids are produced.
Fatty acids are acidic, so the pH of the mixture falls.
An indicator that is pink in alkaline conditions turns colourless as the pH falls.
Digestion products are used to build new carbohydrates, lipids and proteins.
Starch is made of sugar monomers. Proteins are made of amino acids.
Some glucose is used in respiration.
